findings: Tagged SIMD format repeats the roughly 0.8 percent native loss. Whole-process instructions decrease 0.20 percent, cycles increase 0.76 percent, and generic branch misses increase 60.4 percent. The A/A cycle ratio is 1.000046. Increased retired instruction work is excluded; branch behavior is a concrete lead, not yet a branch-address attribution.

AArch64 raw and format execute effectively identical instruction and branch counts but use 0.63 and 0.52 percent more cycles. Branch misses decrease, so a common increased-misprediction explanation for all three losses is contradicted. Format frontend stalls increase about 15.1 percent, but raw frontend change is comparable to A/A variation.
PE32 format retains about 4.2 percent native throughput improvement in this ARM host diagnosis. Existing cross-host losses still prevent publication.
limits: Native and separate PMU groups are different launches. Whole-process counters include unchanged setup and output. Generic branch-misses is not automatically the retired-branch metric described by Arm. Frontend stalls alone do not identify an instruction-cache miss. No sampled hotspot or raw fetch event was collected here; paired bootstrap intervals are descriptive and unadjusted.
